A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same regression-based PPI work by Eyre and Madras. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and expanded scope.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 report original refusal-rate estimation experiments over 350 resamples, including comparisons across LLM subsets. Appendix B reports additional large-label experiments.

after.justification: Section 5 reports original comparisons on research datasets and LLM refusal data. Section 6.5 additionally evaluates adjusted versus unadjusted Sigmoid-PPI.

M1.justification: V2 adds adjusted Sigmoid-PPI, multiplying the sigmoid transformation by 1/(1+n/N) before constructing the estimate (Section 6.5, Equation 18). V1 only discussed the absence of such scaling as a possible failure mechanism. This is a limited inference adaptation of the retained regression-based methods.

E1.justification: V2 adds six research benchmarks: alphafold, ballots, census_healthcare, forest, galaxies, and plankton (Figure 1). These substantially broaden coverage beyond the retained LLM-refusal task, including galaxy-frequency and deforestation estimation.

E2.justification: The main small-label comparisons retain Classical and PPI++ alongside the proposed methods. The large-label comparison changes from Classical, PPI++, Ridge-PPI, and Sigmoid-PPI on refusal data (v1 Figure 3) to Classical and adjusted/unadjusted Sigmoid-PPI on Plankton and Ballots (v2 Figure 5); PPI++ and Ridge-PPI are absent from that comparison.

E3.justification: Refusal-plot axes change from MAE to MSE, although v2 Section 5.2 and captions still specify MAE, leaving the implemented metric unclear. The displayed large-label sweep ends at n=500 instead of n=1000. The stated refusal protocol retains N=1000 and the same small-label regime; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing refusal-subset analysis, v2 adds a cross-dataset correlation between relative estimation error and prediction variance, an analytical variance-sensitivity plot (Figure 4), and an ablation comparing scaled and unscaled Sigmoid-PPI (Figure 5). These substantially expand analysis of failure conditions and the proposed scaling adjustment.

E5.justification: V2 introduces shaded uncertainty bands in Figures 1 and 5, absent from v1, but does not define their statistical meaning or calculation. Both versions specify 350 refusal resamples, so an increased run count is not established. V2 also explicitly qualifies its new correlation as statistically insignificant.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for six research benchmarks, reports Pearson r=-0.69 for its distributional analysis, and evaluates adjusted Sigmoid-PPI at large label counts. Refusal curves have different values and MSE-labelled axes, and the original large-label refusal plot is replaced. These are added or revised results, not established same-metric performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds stochastic-lambda variance analysis, independent-fitting and convergence assumptions, Ridge-PPI excess-risk derivations, and an optimal-ridge-coefficient expression (Sections 6.1–6.4; Appendices B–E). The original regression/MSE equivalence proof is retained, moving from Appendix C to Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the application claim from generative-model auto-evaluation to research-data inference and LLM evaluation. The central claims connecting PPI to regression and proposing Ridge-PPI and Sigmoid-PPI remain. Small-sample PPI failure was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 substantially extends v1's heuristic explanation of low-prediction-variance failures with stochastic-lambda and ridge-risk interpretations. It discusses regularization tradeoffs, difficulty estimating the proposed optimal coefficient, and limitations of the new correlation evidence. The existing large-label Sigmoid limitation is supplemented with an adjustment intended to mitigate it.

D1.justification: The documented finite-sample Ridge-PPI denominator changes from (1+n/N)Var_hat(f)+alpha in v1 Appendix A to (1+n/N)(Var_hat(f)+alpha) in v2 Section 4.4 and Appendix C; whether implementation changed is not established. V2 also documents Ballots-derived moments and a covariance-estimate variance of 0.3/n² for Figure 4.

R1.justification: Section 3 and the bibliography are unchanged. However, Section 6 newly positions the stochastic-lambda analysis as addressing a variance source neglected by previous PPI expressions, modestly expanding the theoretical contribution positioning.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, experiments are subdivided into research and refusal data, and material from v1 Appendices A and B is incorporated into Sections 4.4 and 6.5. Much of the existing background, related-work, and method prose remains unchanged; most expansion consists of separately assessed scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adds a six-panel research figure and a variance contour plot, replaces the large-label refusal figure with two adjusted-Sigmoid comparisons, and redraws the refusal plots with revised axes, legends, grids, and sizing. Shaded bands also introduce a new visual reporting element.

improvement.justification: The broader benchmarks and adjusted-Sigmoid evaluation add useful evidence, but substantial new validity and reporting problems make the net quality direction uncertain. In Appendix B, Equation 26 to 27 incorrectly drops Cov(lambda*b,-lambda*c): under the stated assumptions it equals -Var(lambda)E[f(X)]², undermining Equation 11 and downstream risk analysis. V2 also mixes MSE-labelled plots with MAE descriptions and leaves uncertainty bands undefined. These problems prevent confidently treating the expanded theory and experiments as an overall improvement.
